column8: Thu 19 Nov: store background for rows 7 and 10; rater read Yaniv and Foster 1995 at source (87% agreement across 24 questions, 23 strongly predicted, one tied), but the 0.76 and 0.90 weights were not seen; quiz answers, not a promise of money.
Thu 19 Nov: store, the limit of narrow beats right (13% against 87%, truth 130, verified by the rater in Table 2); Laura never needs the trade after the move, so no report use beyond row 3.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c note for naming the top (after the move every honest wording holds, so the most informative wins); fix the examples: $12-14 million misses the true $15 million, so it is not a case where both hold; keep only 37,000-40,000 against 30,000-45,000 (97%, verified).

Thu 19 Nov: store for 3c or 3d at most a clause; the 1997 sentence (rewards for being informative are immediate) verified by the rater, the candidate and archived-scientist line not re-checked; the she-is-the-scientist turn is clever but needs explaining.
Thu 19 Nov: the movie-theatre line is a suggestion in the paper, untested; the miss-costs-more asymmetry is already Q35-008 (with Q71-005 and Q25-001).

Thu 19 Nov: quote verified by the rater (closing section); 3c reserve beside Neyman, who holds 3c's one outside source (AHA row 1); fix the figure: $117,142 is after the 0.5% margin, so say the room under the top (about 2%, WORDS) or no figure, never $2,142 to spare above what her Treasuries pay with cash earning nothing ($117,731, NUMBERS 3).

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3d one-clause reason to name the top; exact sentence verified by the rater (best point estimate, otherwise the midpoint): unnamed, the range is judged at $105,000 (Keel arithmetic), a figure she never means; the critique's funder-test line misreads framing A, whose readers were told to count the bottom (WHY_A_RANGE 3e).
Thu 19 Nov: 3c, the mechanism behind funder reader 2's margin for error; exact sentence verified by the rater; 3c answers it with Q35-031 (the width is the moved half, money not doubt), one clause.
Thu 19 Nov: store; verified by the rater (43% hit rate, median 17-fold, minimum 5-fold, Exhibit 3); students on quiz questions, so Q11a-035 (managers, 31.2%) and row 15 are the finance versions.

Thu 19 Nov: store only, never scores in the report; arithmetic checks (3.50, 3.00, 1.61; 2.78, 2.28, 1.22), but naming the top gains exactly the midpoint's half-width (10 over 20), so the model restates row 7; the weights and the $5,000 grain are assumptions.
Thu 19 Nov: same congruence point and same use as Rupar's Q35-027 (after the move a bare range reads as mismatched); Du et al. abstract and introduction only; the incongruous quote can join that row.
Thu 19 Nov: same paper and finding as Q11a-033 (preference peaks at a narrow width); the plus or minus 10-20% pilot of 49 was read in a preview only; Laura's plus or minus 9.5% is Keel arithmetic.
Thu 19 Nov: ranges as the usual form of guidance is Q35-017 (with Q11a-034's 80%); NIRI 2016 read through a firm's summary.
Thu 19 Nov: 3c, why finance readers take width as chosen caution, which Q35-031's clause answers; abstracts only (Hribar 2025, Du 2011), so no effect sizes; company earnings, not owned Treasuries.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c clause beside Neyman at most; the rater read the abstract sentence at source (EPS outside the bounds in more than 50 percent of range forecasts; forms not significantly different); abstract only, range and point annual forecasts were under 20% of that sample, so say one 1979-87 sample, and use this or Q11a-035's 31.2%, never both.

Thu 19 Nov: store support for the standing ban on at least $115,000 (Q52); the 69.4% and 1.9% are read via Ciconte's footnote, not the primaries; Pownall's abstract does confirm maximum forecasts' negative price effects.

Thu 19 Nov: the split (23.9% above the top, 36.1% upper half) refines Q11a-035's over 60% from the same survey; these are managers' own internal figures, so never cite them under investors read up (that is Q35-013).
Thu 19 Nov: store; why a missed figure costs belief (69.7%, 59.4%, 56.1%), partly in Q11a-035 (the 46%); managers who guide every quarter, Laura speaks once; never call her bottom a cushion (WORDS).

Thu 19 Nov: abstract only; drop the funder-test parallel: the $95,000 and $115,000 spread was set by the two framings, each telling readers which figure to count, not by a bare range's width (funder test RESULTS).

Thu 19 Nov: 3d reserve for its two parts with two dates (WHY_A_RANGE 4c); abstract only, no effect sizes; earnings line items, not dated holdings; 3d carries one clause of evidence at most (Gneezy and Epley or the better-estimate rule), so this does not join them.
Thu 19 Nov: field support for row 20's disaggregation point; abstract only.
Thu 19 Nov: 3e caution, synopsis only: never claim research shows a range beats a point.
Thu 19 Nov: store; abstracts only; students pricing gambles, and co-sponsors are boards that budget, so it qualifies listeners hear the top only for lay supporters.
Thu 19 Nov: store; chances in urn games, serves no part.
Thu 19 Nov: same group and same point as row 23 (attitudes to vagueness depend on the frame); abstract only.

Thu 19 Nov: the which-outcome finding (certain pulls to the low end, possible to the high) is already Q71-001 with Q71-002's advice; abstract only; it backs WORDS's rule that certain takes the stated range as its subject.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d voice: the figure, then its two parts with their dates, in full sentences (voice round 8); a new quote from Teigen 2023, already Q19-027's source; Laura's figure is owned, not uncertain, so take the habit, not the premise.

Thu 19 Nov: coherence check for 3c, 3d and Table 2's note (one frame: the top as her figure, the bottom as the part held since January 2028); abstract only; Table 2's before-the-move percentages answer another question and keep their own label.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d evidence for naming the top; Study 1 verified by the rater ($77.01 to $68.15, deal $83.72 to $72.87, bolstering $83.26 and $89.14); never call Laura's range backdown: her lower figure is no concession to co-sponsors, so in Ames and Mason's terms it is the speaker-favouring side, and the pull toward the extra figure holds either way; drop the funder-test support (framing A told readers to count the bottom); a price haggle, not a gift.

Thu 19 Nov: Study 3's $67.65 against $71.58 verified by the rater; the 29% and 17% pilot shares and the phrase generally ill-advised were not found in the article text read (attribute the phrase to Shonk's PON page or drop it); 3d note only.
Thu 19 Nov: restates row 29's use with the worker brief's ban on a stated contribution above the stated top.
Thu 19 Nov: the 3.6 times restates Q35-029, whose source is Cheng et al. (2013), not Ciconte; Ames and Mason's over 80% of range offers 5-25% wide was verified by the rater and can join that row.
Thu 19 Nov: the quote is about donors choosing from an ask range; carrying it to co-sponsors booking a giver's own stated range is Keel inference and must say so; a practitioner's belief, not a test.
Thu 19 Nov: store; asks to donors, not a giver's statement; supports one figure for a commitment only by inference.
Thu 19 Nov: store; mailed appeals for small gifts, abstract only, serves no part.
Thu 19 Nov: store; consistent with the funder test, where readers booked the figure they were told to count under either framing; asks to givers, not a giver's statement.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c note for why no reading convention can be assumed; drop the funder test from the budgeters' evidence (framing A told readers to count the bottom, WHY_A_RANGE 3e), and investors read up rests on Q35-013, not row 17 (managers' own figures).
Thu 19 Nov: 3c checklist for option (b) (each end backed and shown, width explained, one frame); restates WHY_A_RANGE 4b with sources; no study compares an owned range with a point.
Thu 19 Nov: restates WHY_A_RANGE option (b) and Q71-033's record of what was owned first; its $20,000 per co-sponsor came from framing A telling readers to count the bottom, not from a bare range.
Thu 19 Nov: IPS l.15 read whole is WHY_A_RANGE 2a and Q19-028 (a range of choice, all owned); the IPS says VT's returns will help determine her maximum, never that VT sets it.
